abstract_en:
Background
Exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are followed by a marked and sustained increase in cardiovascular risk, and anti-type 2 biologics reduce exacerbations in eosinophilic COPD. Whether these agents modify cardiovascular outcomes is unknown.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched to 31 October 2026 for phase 3, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of anti-type 2 biologics in eosinophilic COPD. The primary outcome was independently adjudicated 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Data were pooled with the fixed-effect Peto method. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was performed to assess the conclusiveness of the available evidence and estimate the sample size needed to detect a treatment effect, assuming a two-sided α of 5% and 80% power.Results
Seven trials met the eligibility criteria. Three (BOREAS, NOTUS and MATINEE; 2676 patients; 45 events) reported adjudicated MACE, whereas adjudicated MACE from GALATHEA and TERRANOVA were not reported. Biologic therapy was associated with a numerical but non-significant reduction in MACE (Peto odds ratio [OR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.37-1.19; p = 0.17; I2 = 0%; very low certainty). Estimates were OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.20-1.03) with interleukin (IL)-4/IL-13 blockade by dupilumab and OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.43-2.32) with IL-5 blockade by mepolizumab, with no evidence of a difference between molecular targets (test for subgroup differences, p = 0.19). The accrued information (2676 patients) was 24% of the required information size (10,959 patients).Conclusions
Current phase 3 evidence does not establish a cardiovascular effect of anti-type 2 biologics in eosinophilic COPD. Standardized cardiovascular-risk assessment and prospectively adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes are needed in future biologic trials.

abstract_en:
Background
Cancer is increasingly common among patients with cardiovascular disease, yet representation of patients with cancer in cardiovascular randomized controlled trials (RCTs) is unclear. We assessed cancer-related eligibility criteria and reporting practices in major cardiovascular RCTs.Methods
We systematically reviewed RCTs (≥ 500 participants) enrolling adults with coronary artery disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke, peripheral artery disease or valvular heart disease (2000-2025). Trials were identified from ClinicalTrials.gov, bibliographic databases and trial registries. Studies were classified based on cancer-related eligibility criteria and reporting practices. Clinical endpoints were required according to international consensus definitions. Predictors of cancer exclusion were evaluated using logistic regression, and pooled cancer prevalence was estimated using mixed-effects models.Results
We included 863 RCTs (n = 3,435,447). Overall, 11.9% explicitly excluded all patients with cancer, while 50.2% did not report cancer prevalence and specified nonspecific life-expectancy or comorbidity restrictions potentially affecting patients with cancer. Only 5.2% reported any cancer prevalence. Exclusion was highest in hypertension (36.4%) and diabetes (29.2%) trials and lowest in coronary artery disease (8.6%) and atrial fibrillation (8.2%) trials. More recent publication year was associated with higher odds of exclusion (adjusted OR 1.08 per year; p Conclusions
Explicit cancer exclusion and limited reporting of cancer prevalence were common in cardiovascular RCTs. Differences in reported prevalence between trial and observational populations warrant further investigation using harmonized populations and cancer definitions.Trial registration

abstract_en:
Background
Combination of antiplatelet therapy (APT) and anticoagulation is common and influences the risk-benefit of anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.Methods
COMBINE-AF (A Collaboration Between Multiple Institutions to Better Investigate Non-Vitamin K Antagonist Oral Anticoagulant Use in Atrial Fibrillation) is an individual patient-data meta-analysis of 4 randomized trials comparing direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with warfarin. Baseline APT was administered at the treating physician's discretion. Primary analyses assessed the association of baseline APT and treatment-effect modification of standard-dose DOACs versus warfarin on stroke or systemic embolic events and major bleeding.Results
Of 57 598 patients enrolled, 19 774 (34.3%) received APT at baseline (>90% aspirin monotherapy). Compared with non-APT users, those on APT had similar age and were more commonly men, with greater prevalence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. After multivariable adjustment and irrespective of randomization arm, patients receiving APT had a higher hazard of stroke/systemic embolic events (adjusted hazard ratio [HRadj], 1.17 [95% CI, 1.07-1.29]; Padj, 1.38 [95% CI, 1.28-1.48]; PPint=0.27) and major bleeding (no APT: HR, 0.85 [95% CI, 0.77-0.93]; APT: HR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.78-0.98]; Pint=0.64) to a similar degree with and without APT. Secondary analyses revealed a consistent benefit with DOACs versus warfarin for reduction of fatal and intracranial bleeding irrespective of APT use, but an increase in major gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly in older patients on APT.Conclusions
DOACs offer consistent benefits over warfarin, reducing stroke/systemic embolic events and major bleeding irrespective of baseline antiplatelet use. In patients on oral anticoagulants, APT should be restricted to those with a clear indication.

abstract_en:
Introduction
Administering lactate to critically ill patients or patients undergoing major surgery may improve hemodynamics, reduce intracranial pressure and decrease fluid requirements. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to analyze whether these beneficial effects also translate into mortality reduction.Methods
We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing lactate infusion against any control in adult patients having critical illness or undergoing major surgery. Primary outcome was mortality at the last reported follow-up. Data on other clinical outcomes (length of stay, survival with good neurological outcome, adverse events), and hemodynamic data (heart rate, blood pressure, cardiac output, fluid balance) were also extracted.Results
A total of ten RCTs with a total of 763 patients were included. All studies investigated hypertonic sodium lactate (HSL), compared against isotonic or hypertonic fluids. Investigated settings included acute cardiovascular care (cardiac and aortic surgery, acute heart failure), severe burn injury and traumatic brain injury. Mortality was similar in all settings but has to be taken as hypothesis generating due to the very low number of trials. We found no difference in other secondary outcomes.Conclusions
Hypertonic sodium lactate did not demonstrate a mortality difference, but administering HSL appeared to be safe, as no adverse events were reported. Overall, our findings have to be considered hypothesis-generating rather than practice changing due to the very small sample size and different populations.Study registration
International prospective register of systematic reviews, PROSPERO registration no. CRD420251124739.

abstract_en:
Objective
This review aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes of open (conventional arch repair, frozen elephant trunk), endovascular based treatment, hybrid, and conservative management for non-A non-B aortic dissection.Data sources
MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 September 2025, with a supplementary search for conservatively managed cohorts.Review methods
This was a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions of non-randomised observational studies, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD42024534559). English language cohort studies and case series of ≥ 15 adult patients with non-A non-B dissection reporting predefined outcomes were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). Proportions were pooled separately within each modality (random effects, logit transformation). No between modality comparison was made. Sensitivity analyses comprised leave one out, influence diagnostics, and a generalised linear mixed model. Certainty was rated using GRADE.Results
Eighteen studies comprising 1 062 patients (mean age 55 years, 82% men) were included; 1 019 contributed to the pooled estimates. Pooled in hospital mortality was 4.6% (95% CI 2.2 - 9.6) after endovascular based treatment, 5.5% (2.6 - 11.3) after frozen elephant trunk, 7.8% (4.2 - 14.3) after hybrid repair, and 11.1% (4.0 - 27.1) with conservative management, with widely overlapping confidence intervals. Stroke ranged from 3.9% after endovascular based treatment to 9.7% with conservative management. Over 12 - 60 months mean follow up, cumulative mortality after discharge ranged from 3.1% (frozen elephant trunk) to 15.0% (conservative management), with 33.4% crossover to intervention. Retrograde type A dissection followed only stent graft based strategies (endovascular based treatment 3.4%); endoleak affected 15.7% of endovascular based treatment and 13.4% of hybrid patients. Certainty was very low overall.Conclusion
In this synthesis, in hospital mortality was below 10% after endovascular based treatment, frozen elephant trunk and hybrid repair, each with a distinct complication profile relevant to treatment selection. These single arm proportions derive from populations selected by anatomy and operative fitness and are of very low certainty, and do not support estimation of comparative treatment effects.

abstract_en:
Background
Hypertension is the most prevalent modifiable cardiovascular risk factor among adults living with HIV, and cardiovascular disease has displaced AIDS-defining illness as the leading cause of death in many settings. Although pharmacological, lifestyle, and health-system interventions have been implemented to improve blood pressure control, their comparative effectiveness remains unclear. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) compared and ranked interventions for blood pressure control among adults with HIV.Methods
A systematic search of MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, WHO Global Index Medicus, WHO ICTRP, ClinicalTrials.gov, and supplementary sources was conducted from inception to 10 May 2026. Randomised controlled trials evaluating blood pressure-lowering strategies in adults living with HIV were eligible. Random-effects frequentist NMA was performed using the netmeta package in R. Primary outcomes were changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Interventions were grouped by the randomised contrast into pharmacological, lifestyle and care-delivery strategies, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE for network meta-analysis.Results
Database searches identified 3,958 records; 14 randomised controlled trials (13,204 participants, 10 countries) were included, of which nine (5,082 participants) contributed to the systolic blood pressure (SBP) network and four (2,613) to the diastolic blood pressure (DBP) network. Calcium channel blockers (CCB), evaluated in a single trial of 242 adults with prehypertension, reduced SBP compared with control (mean difference [MD] -5.89 mmHg; 95% CI -9.03 to -2.75; low certainty). Care-delivery strategies (six trials, 4,743 participants) reduced SBP (MD -1.51 mmHg; 95% CI -2.70 to -0.32; low certainty); the estimate for lifestyle interventions (two trials, 97 participants) was -4.44 mmHg (95% CI -9.64 to 0.75; very low certainty). All comparisons between active interventions were indirect, and CCB and lifestyle interventions did not differ (MD -1.45 mmHg; 95% CI -7.52 to 4.63). No intervention significantly reduced DBP, for which heterogeneity was considerable (I2 = 79%).Conclusions
Randomised evidence on blood pressure-lowering interventions specific to people with HIV is limited. A single trial supports amlodipine in adults with prehypertension receiving dolutegravir-based therapy, and care-delivery strategies produce small but consistent reductions in systolic blood pressure. The data do not show that any intervention is superior to another; adequately powered trials of antihypertensive treatment in people with HIV and established hypertension, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, are needed.

abstract_en:
Aims
Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) treat severe aortic stenosis. Although cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves functional recovery, its association with mortality remains unclear. We aimed to assess this association in adults following TAVI or SAVR.Methods
PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 17, 2026. We included randomized and observational studies comparing mortality after CR versus usual care following TAVI or SAVR. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses and exploratory meta-regressions were performed.Results
A total of 7 observational studies (n=178,525 participants) were included (six pooled; n=92,213), all focusing on all-cause mortality. Participants reported mean or median ages ranged from 67 to 83.9 years, with 37-66.7% women across studies. All studies were deemed to have a high methodological quality. Pooled results revealed that CR was associated with a lower all-cause mortality risk compared to control groups (HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.41-0.84], p=0.004; I2=95%). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results, as did sub-analyses restricted to TAVI participants (HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.50-0.92], p=0.012). No sub-analysis could be performed for SAVR participants alone. Exploratory meta-regression analyses found no statistically significant associations between studies' characteristics (e.g., patients' age, CR duration, follow-up length) and effect estimates (all p>0.05), although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies.Conclusion
Participation in CR after TAVI/SAVR is associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Future studies should determine whether participants' or interventions' characteristics modulate these effects.

abstract_en: Abstract  Emergency physicians must balance timely treatment of bacterial infection against unnecessary antibiotic prescribing. We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials evaluating whether procalcitonin-guided care changes initial antibiotic initiation or prescription in adults presenting to emergency departments with suspected infection. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception through August 25, 2026. Trials were pooled when outcome definitions were sufficiently comparable, using random-effects meta-analysis with modified Hartung–Knapp confidence intervals. Ten trials (13,286 participants) were included; four respiratory infection trials (3,602 participants) contributed to the primary synthesis. Procalcitonin-guided care reduced initial antibiotic initiation or prescription (risk ratio, 0.87; 95% confidence interval, 0.82–0.92; I²=0%; high-certainty evidence), corresponding to approximately 89 fewer patients receiving or being prescribed antibiotics per 1,000. Sensitivity analyses produced similar estimates. For 28- to 30-day mortality, the pooled risk ratio across five trials was 0.92 (95% confidence interval, 0.57–1.49; low-certainty evidence); estimates for intensive care unit admission and antibiotic-related adverse events were imprecise. This updated review provides a decision-specific estimate of reduced initial antibiotic prescribing in emergency department respiratory infections and clarifies how differences in outcome definitions, trial designs, and patient populations affect interpretation of earlier syntheses. Effects on mortality and other clinical outcomes remain uncertain overall, and the respiratory prescribing estimate should not be extrapolated to undifferentiated fever, suspected sepsis, or acute heart failure.

abstract_en:
Background
Whether protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies provide incremental benefit beyond contemporary usual care remains uncertain. The authors performed a Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized trials in major noncardiac surgery.Methods
MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to January 5, 2026, with additional literature surveillance through June 29, 2026. Randomized trials comparing protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies with usual care or lower-pressure approaches were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS). Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis was prespecified as the primary analytical framework, with confirmatory frequentist analyses.Results
Fifteen randomized trials met the inclusion criteria. Mortality (13 trials) remained centered around an odds ratio (OR) of 1.00 (frequentist OR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.21; Bayesian median OR, 1.00; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.73 to 1.38), with wide Bayesian prediction intervals (OR, 0.56 to1.78). AKI (14 trials) showed the most favorable estimates (frequentist OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; Bayesian median OR, 0.88; 95% CrI, 0.70 to 1.05), but estimates remained compatible with no clinically important benefit, heterogeneity was moderate, and leave-one-out analyses, excluding each trial in turn, showed sensitivity to individual trial exclusion. MINS (eight trials) likewise remained compatible with no treatment effect (frequentist OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.15; Bayesian median OR, 1.05; 95% CrI, 0.90 to 1.26). Exploratory analyses suggested that any potential renal benefit may depend on the broader hemodynamic context in which arterial pressure targets are implemented.Conclusions
Protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies did not demonstrate a consistent incremental benefit over contemporary usual care in major noncardiac surgery. Mortality and MINS remained compatible with no treatment effect. Although AKI showed the most favorable estimates, the evidence remained uncertain, was sensitive to individual trial exclusion, and should be interpreted cautiously.

El resultado primario fue mortalidad por todas las causas; los resultados secundarios fueron lesión renal aguda (AKI) y lesión miocárdica después de cirugía no cardiaca (MINS).El metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios bayesianos se preespecificó como el marco analítico primario, con análisis frecuente confirmatorio.Resultados Quince ensayos aleatorizados cumplieron los criterios de inclusión.La mortalidad (13 ensayos) se mantuvo centrada alrededor de una proporción de probabilidades (OR) de 1,00 (OR frecuente, 1,00; IC 95%, 0,83 a 1,21; mediana de OR bayesiana, 1,00; intervalo creíble del 95% [CrI], 0,73 a 1,38), con amplios intervalos de predicción bayesiana (OR, 0,56 a 1,78). La AKI (14 ensayos) mostró las estimaciones más favorables (OR frecuente, 0,87; IC 95%, 0,73 a 1,03; OR mediana bayesiana, 0,88; IC 95%, 0,70 a 1,05), pero las estimaciones siguieron siendo compatibles sin beneficio clínicamente importante, la heterogeneidad fue moderada y los análisis de exclusión individual, excluyendo cada ensayo a su vez, mostraron sensibilidad a la exclusión individual del ensayo; el MNS (ocho ensayos) también siguió siendo compatible sin efecto terapéutico (OR frecuente, 1,04; IC 95%, 0,93 a 1,15; OR mediana bayesiana, 1,05; IC 95%, 0,90 a 1,26). Los análisis exploratorios sugieren que cualquier beneficio renal potencial puede depender del contexto hemodinámico más amplio en el que se implementan los objetivos de presión arterial.Conclusiones Las estrategias de focalización de presión arterial intraoperatoria protocolar no demostraron un beneficio incremental consistente sobre la atención habitual contemporánea en cirugía no cardiaca mayor.La mortalidad y el MNS permanecieron compatibles sin efecto terapéutico.Aunque la AKI mostró las estimaciones más favorables, la evidencia permaneció incierta, fue sensible a la exclusión de ensayos individuales y debe interpretarse con cautela.

abstract_en:
Background
Saphenous vein graft (SVG) occlusion remains common after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) despite aspirin. We compared contemporary postoperative antithrombotic regimens for preserving SVG patency.Methods
We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 2026. The primary outcome was graft-level SVG occlusion. Aspirin was the reference treatment. Inconsistency was assessed using design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting. Because multiple SVGs could arise from the same patient, we added a post-hoc variance-inflation sensitivity analysis using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.15, 0.20, and 0.25.Results
Fifteen trials met review criteria; 10 contributed to the primary network (6,934 SVGs, 22 treatment arms, 7 nodes). Aspirin plus ticagrelor reduced SVG occlusion versus aspirin alone (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34-0.80; p = 0.003). Aspirin plus clopidogrel showed a non-significant possible benefit (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38-1.04; p = 0.070). Other regimens were not significantly different from aspirin. Aspirin plus ticagrelor ranked highest (P-score 0.88). Heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 52.6%). The aspirin plus ticagrelor finding remained significant after clustering variance inflation across ICCs 0.15-0.25 (adjusted OR approximately 0.53; all p ≤ 0.006).Conclusions
Aspirin plus ticagrelor was associated with lower graft-level SVG occlusion, but SVG patency is a surrogate outcome. Randomized evidence has not established corresponding reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events or mortality, while intensified dual antiplatelet therapy may increase bleeding. Treatment should therefore be individualized.Registration
This review was not prospectively registered. An a posteriori protocol and data repository was archived on OSF after screening and analysis had commenced: https://osf.io/qfwc9/.

title: When does personalization matter? An evidence-to-action beyond smart devices demonstrating the added clinical value of personalization in precision MedTech.
short: When does personalization matter? An evidence-to-action beyond smart devices demonstrating the added clinical value of personalization in precision MedTech.
summary: Antecedentes La medicina de precisión (PM) busca mejorar la prevención, el diagnóstico y el tratamiento mediante la incorporación de variaciones biológicas, clínicas, ambientales y conductuales en lugar de depender exclusivamente de los promedios poblacionales. La tecnología médica (MedTech) proporciona una interfaz práctica a través de la cual este enfoque puede traducirse en detección continua, apoyo a la decisión e intervención individualizada.

authors: Qoronfleh MW.
abstract_en:
Background
Precision medicine (PM) seeks to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment by incorporating biologic, clinical, environmental, and behavioral variation rather than relying exclusively on population averages. Medical technology (MedTech) provides a practical interface through which this approach can be translated into continuous sensing, decision support, and individualized intervention. We use the term personalized/precision medical devices (PMDs) for a conceptual class of devices that combine person-specific inputs with analytics and device-level configuration or adaptation. PMDs overlap with smart devices, connected health, and digital therapeutics, but are distinguished by their explicit coupling of individualized data to clinically meaningful device behavior.Methods
This perspective uses a structured narrative literature approach. The literature survey was extended through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and major regulatory/standards sources for publications addressing precision or personalized medicine, biosensing, wearable and implantable devices, point-of-care diagnostics, automated drug delivery, digital therapeutics, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), interoperability, regulation, cybersecurity, and health equity [Oct. 2025-Oct. 2026]. Preference was given to peer-reviewed clinical studies, systematic reviews, authoritative regulatory guidance, and international standards. Evidence was synthesized narratively around a device lifecycle framework linking individual profile, sensing, data infrastructure, analytics, actuation, clinical workflow, evidence generation, and governance.Results
Clinical evidence demonstrates that some components of the PMD concept are already established. In a randomized trial, automated insulin delivery increased time in the target glucose range by 14% points versus sensor-augmented pump therapy at 24 weeks. Remote pulmonary-artery pressure monitoring reduced heart-failure hospitalization by 28% in a prespecified analysis of patients with reduced ejection fraction. In the Apple Heart Study, 419,297 participants were enrolled; 0.52% received an irregular-pulse notification, and atrial fibrillation was identified in 34% of participants who returned an analyzable electrocardiographic patch. Digital therapeutics and adaptive neurostimulation further illustrate how software and implantable systems can individualize treatment, although clinical generalizability and long-term evidence remain uneven.Conclusions
PMDs should be viewed as an engineering and clinical integration paradigm, not as a new regulatory category. Their value depends less on novelty of individual components than on reliable linkage among person-specific data, clinically validated algorithms, device actuation, and longitudinal feedback. Translation therefore requires evidence generation, interoperability, cybersecurity, lifecycle regulation, accountable AI, and equity-by-design. The next phase of precision MedTech will be defined by selective deployment of these capabilities where individualized sensing and adaptation demonstrably improve clinical outcomes or care efficiency.

Las DMP se superponen con dispositivos inteligentes, salud conectada y terapéutica digital, pero se distinguen por su acoplamiento explícito de datos individualizados al comportamiento del dispositivo clínicamente significativo.Métodos Esta perspectiva utiliza un enfoque de literatura narrativa estructurada. La encuesta de literatura se amplió mediante búsquedas dirigidas a PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, y las principales fuentes normativas/estándares para publicaciones que abordan la medicina de precisión o personalizada, biosensibilización, dispositivos portátiles e implantables, diagnósticos de puntos de cuidado, entrega automatizada de fármacos, terapia digital, inteligencia artificial (AI), Internet of Medical Things (IOMT), interoperabilidad, regulación, ciberseguridad y equidad en salud [Oct. 2025-Oct. 2026]. Se dio preferencia a estudios clínicos revisados por pares, revisiones sistemáticas, orientación normativa autorizada y normas internacionales. La evidencia fue sintetizada narrativamente en torno a un marco de ciclo de vida del dispositivo que vincula el perfil individual, la detección, la infraestructura de datos, la analítica, la actuación, el flujo de trabajo clínico, la generación de evidencia y la gobernanza.Resultados La evidencia clínica demuestra que algunos componentes del concepto de DMP ya están establecidos.En un ensayo aleatorizado, la administración automatizada de insulina aumentó el tiempo en el rango de glucosa objetivo en un 14% puntos frente a la terapia con bomba aumentada por sensores a las 24 semanas. En el Apple Heart Study se incluyeron 419.297 participantes; el 0,52% recibió una notificación de pulso irregular y se identificó fibrilación auricular en el 34% de los participantes que devolvieron un parche electrocardiográfico analizable. La terapia digital y la neuroestimulación adaptativa ilustran aún más cómo el software y los sistemas implantables pueden individualizar el tratamiento, aunque la generalización clínica y la evidencia a largo plazo siguen siendo desiguales.Conclusiones Las DMP deben considerarse como un paradigma de ingeniería e integración clínica, no como una nueva categoría reguladora. Su valor depende menos de la novedad de los componentes individuales que de la vinculación fiable entre datos específicos de cada persona, algoritmos validados clínicamente, activación de dispositivos y retroalimentación longitudinal. Por lo tanto, la traducción requiere generación de evidencia, interoperabilidad, ciberseguridad, regulación del ciclo de vida, IA responsable y equidad por diseño. La próxima fase de precisión MedTech se definirá mediante el despliegue selectivo de estas capacidades donde la detección individualizada y la adaptación demuestran mejorar los resultados clínicos o la eficiencia del cuidado.

abstract_en: Background Cardiovascular diseases remain one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and heart failure (HF) represents a major global public health challenge, affecting an estimated 64 million people globally. The pathophysiology of HF is multifactorially complex and poorly understood. Understanding the role of inflammation in relation to CA125 levels will consolidate and enhance their clinical and prognostic value in the risk assessment, stratification and clinical management of HF. Hence, this review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of the available evidence on the relationship between immune-inflammatory activation and circulating CA125 concentrations in heart failure. Methods An extensive search will be conducted on the following databases: MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. The Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) and Cochrane Central Register of Clinical Trials (CENTRAL) will also be searched. Two reviewers will independently screen studies for eligibility using predefined criteria. The quality assessment and risk of bias of included studies will be assessed using the modified Downs and Black’s checklist. The Review Manager will be used for statistical analysis. The overall quality of included studies will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation assessment tool. Discussions In HF management, biomarkers are essential for accurate diagnosis and risk stratification. CA125 has emerged as a key link between clinical congestion, immune-inflammatory activation, and adverse patient outcomes; however, current evidence regarding its inflammatory trigger remains fragmented. This review explores whether inflammatory pathways drive CA125 elevation independently of mechanical congestion, establishing its clinical utility and biological significance alongside conventional HF biomarkers. Ethics, patient and public involvement This is a review of existing studies and will not require ethical approval. Hence, patients and the public will not be involved in the study. abstract_en: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is one of the most frequent and consequential complications of maintenance hemodialysis, affecting up to 40% of treatments depending on the definition used. IDH is independently associated with myocardial stunning, cerebral hypoperfusion, loss of residual kidney function, vascular access failure, and increased mortality. Despite extensive investigation, heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and reliance on intermittent blood pressure measurements continue to limit prevention and management. We performed a narrative review of clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and guideline statements addressing intradialytic hypotension in adult hemodialysis populations. Evidence was synthesized across pathophysiologic mechanisms, monitoring strategies, and therapeutic approaches, including conventional and digital health interventions. IDH arises from an interplay of ultrafiltration-plasma refill mismatch, impaired vascular responses, reduced cardiac reserve, osmotic and thermal shifts, and medication effects. Epidemiologic estimates vary due to inconsistent definitions, although a nadir systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg shows the strongest and consistent association with mortality. Traditional intermittent cuff-based blood pressure monitoring underestimates the burden and severity of IDH. Advanced monitoring approaches, including continuous noninvasive blood pressure measurement, volume assessment tools, and integrated dialysis machine feedback systems, enable improved detection of subclinical and evolving hypotension. Recent machine learning and artificial intelligence models leveraging clinical and real-time intradialytic data demonstrate strong performance for IDH prediction and support individualized ultrafiltration and dry weight optimization. Overall, IDH remains a multifactorial and under-recognized driver of morbidity in hemodialysis patients, and integration of precision monitoring with AI-enabled analytics may improve hemodynamic stability and clinical outcomes.
abstract_es: Abstract

La hipotensión intradialítica (HID) es una de las complicaciones más frecuentes y consecuentes de la hemodiálisis de mantenimiento, afectando hasta el 40% de los tratamientos dependiendo de la definición utilizada. La IDH se asocia de forma independiente con aturdimiento miocárdico, hipoperfusión cerebral, pérdida de la función renal residual, insuficiencia del acceso vascular y aumento de la mortalidad. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de ensayos clínicos, estudios observacionales, revisiones sistemáticas e indicaciones orientativas que abordan la hipotensión intradialítica en poblaciones de hemodiálisis adultas. La evidencia fue sintetizada a través de mecanismos fisiopatológicos, estrategias de monitoreo y abordajes terapéuticos, incluyendo intervenciones de salud convencionales y digitales. La IDH surge de una interacción de desajuste de recarga ultrafiltración-plasma, respuestas vasculares deterioradas, reducción de la reserva cardíaca, cambios osmóticos y térmicos y efectos de medicación. Las estimaciones epidemiológicas varían debido a definiciones incoherentes, aunque una presión arterial sistólica nadir inferior a 90 mmHg muestra la asociación más fuerte y consistente con la mortalidad. La monitorización intermitente tradicional de la presión arterial basada en manguitos subestima la carga y gravedad de la IDH. Los enfoques avanzados de monitorización, incluyendo medición continua de la presión arterial no invasiva, herramientas de evaluación de volumen y sistemas integrados de retroalimentación de la máquina de diálisis, permiten una mejor detección de hipotensión subclínica y en evolución. Los recientes modelos de aprendizaje automático e inteligencia artificial que aprovechan datos clínicos y intradialíticos en tiempo real demuestran un fuerte rendimiento para la predicción de IDH y apoyan la ultrafiltración individualizada y la optimización del peso seco. En general, IDH sigue siendo un motor multifactorial y poco reconocido de morbilidad en pacientes hemodiálisis, y la integración de la monitorización de precisión con análisis con IA puede mejorar la estabilidad hemodinámica y los resultados clínicos.

title: Clinical Outcomes Associated With Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract_en: The optimal strategy for managing concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. We performed an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative or deferred management in patients with CAD undergoing TAVI. Major electronic databases were systematically searched for eligible RCTs. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model, with sensitivity analyses performed to assess robustness and explore the influence of individual studies on heterogeneity. Three RCTs were included. Routine PCI was not associated with a significant reduction in mortality or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with conservative or deferred management. However, PCI was associated with significantly higher risks of major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.33; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P < 0.001), while urgent revascularization was less frequent with PCI. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that individual studies influenced heterogeneity for selected outcomes, although the overall findings remained broadly consistent. Among patients with CAD undergoing TAVI, this pooled analysis of the available randomized evidence shows that an unselective, routine strategy of PCI does not reduce mortality, myocardial infarction, or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with a conservative or deferred strategy, while increasing bleeding and reducing the subsequent need for urgent revascularization. Rather than indicating that coronary intervention is unnecessary, these findings clarify the precision and consistency of this tradeoff across the available trials and support a selective, individualized strategy in which PCI is reserved for clinically or physiologically significant coronary disease rather than performed routinely on the basis of angiographic appearance alone.

La estrategia óptima para el manejo de la enfermedad coronaria concomitante (CAD) en pacientes sometidos a implante valvular aórtico transcatéter (TAVI) sigue siendo incierta. Se realizó un metanálisis actualizado de ensayos controlados aleatorizados (TRC) comparando la intervención coronaria percutánea (ICP) con el manejo conservador o diferido en pacientes con EAC sometidos a TAVI. Se buscaron sistemáticamente bases de datos electrónicas importantes para la detección de ECA elegibles. Las relaciones de riesgo (RR) con intervalos de confianza (IC) del 95% se agruparon utilizando un modelo de efectos aleatorios, con análisis de sensibilidad realizados para evaluar la robustez y explorar la influencia de estudios individuales sobre la heterogeneidad. La ICP rutinaria no se asoció con una reducción significativa de la mortalidad o de los eventos cardiovasculares y cerebrovasculares adversos mayores en comparación con el manejo conservador o diferido; sin embargo, la ICP se asoció con riesgos significativamente mayores de hemorragia mayor (RR, 1,57; IC 95%, 1,06-2,33; P = 0,02) y cualquier sangrado (RR, 1,77; IC 95%, 1,27-2,48; P < 0,001), mientras que la revascularización urgente fue menos frecuente con la ICP. Los análisis de sensibilidad demostraron que los estudios individuales influyeron en la heterogeneidad de los resultados seleccionados, aunque los hallazgos globales se mantuvieron ampliamente consistentes. Entre los pacientes con EAC sometidos a TAVI, este análisis agrupado de la evidencia aleatoria disponible muestra que una estrategia no selectiva y rutinaria de ICP no reduce la mortalidad, infarto de miocardio o eventos cardiovasculares y cerebrovasculares adversos mayores en comparación con una estrategia conservadora o diferida, al tiempo que aumenta el sangrado y reduce la necesidad posterior de revascularización urgente. En lugar de indicar que la intervención coronaria es innecesaria, estos hallazgos aclaran la precisión y la consistencia de este equilibrio en los ensayos disponibles y apoyan una estrategia selectiva e individualizada en la que la ICP está reservada a la enfermedad coronaria clínicamente o fisiológicamente significativa en lugar de realizarse rutinariamente sobre la base de la apariencia angiográfica sola.

abstract_en: Heart failure (HF) carries high morbidity and mortality, and the prognostic role of serum magnesium remains unclear. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis assessed associations between magnesium abnormalities and outcomes in HF. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through March 2026 for observational cohorts, registries, and post hoc randomized controlled trial analyses in adults with HF. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were HF hospitalization and cardiovascular (CV) mortality. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool and the revised Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool for Randomized Trials. Twelve studies including 648,602 patients were analyzed. Hypermagnesemia was associated with higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.32-1.44; I2 = 6%), HF hospitalization (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51; I2 = 81%), and CV mortality (RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.19-1.66; I2 = 42%). Hypomagnesemia was associated with modestly higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01-1.31; I2 = 70%), with no significant association with HF hospitalization or CV death. Associations were consistent across studies published before and after 2010 and between observational cohorts and post hoc trial analyses, with no significant subgroup differences. The association between hypermagnesemia and all-cause mortality was unchanged after excluding the largest study (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.25-1.53; I2 = 13%). Serum magnesium abnormalities, especially hypermagnesemia, are associated with worse outcomes in HF. Hypomagnesemia shows a smaller, less consistent association. Because hypermagnesemia may largely reflect renal dysfunction and greater disease severity, these findings represent prognostic associations rather than evidence of causality; prospective studies should determine whether monitoring or correcting magnesium abnormalities improves HF outcomes.
abstract_es: Abstract

La insuficiencia cardíaca (IC) conlleva una alta morbilidad y mortalidad, y el papel pronóstico del magnesio sérico sigue sin estar claro. Esta revisión sistemática actualizada y la evaluación de las asociaciones meta-análisis entre las anomalías del magnesio y los resultados en IC. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science y Cochrane fueron buscados hasta marzo de 2026 en busca de cohortes observacionales, registros y análisis de ensayos controlados post hoc aleatorios en adultos con IC. El resultado primario fue mortalidad por todas las causas; los resultados secundarios fueron hospitalización por IC y mortalidad cardiovascular (CV). Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando la herramienta de Estudios de Calidad en el Pronóstico y la herramienta revisada de Cochrane Risk-of-Bias para Ensayos Aleatorizados. Se analizaron 12 estudios que incluyeron 648.602 pacientes. La hipermagnesemia se asoció con mayor mortalidad por todas las causas (RR 1,38, IC 95% 1,32-1,44; I2 = 6%), hospitalización por IC (RR 1,30, IC 95% 1,11-1,51; I2 = 81%) y mortalidad CV (RR 1,41, IC 95% 1,19-1,66; I2 = 42%). La hipomagnesemia se asoció con mortalidad por todas las causas (RR 1,15, IC 95% 1,01-1,31; I2 = 70%), sin asociación significativa con hospitalización por IC o muerte por CV. Las asociaciones fueron consistentes entre los estudios publicados antes y después de 2010 y entre cohortes observacionales y análisis post hoc, sin diferencias significativas entre subgrupos; la asociación entre hipermagnesemia y mortalidad por todas las causas se mantuvo inalterada después de excluir el estudio más grande (RR 1,38, IC 95% 1,25-1,53; I2 = 13%). Las anomalías séricas de magnesio, especialmente la hipermagnesemia, se asocian con peores resultados en IC. La hipomagnesemia muestra una asociación menor y menos consistente. Debido a que la hipermagnesemia puede reflejar en gran medida la disfunción renal y una mayor gravedad de la enfermedad, estos hallazgos representan asociaciones pronósticas en lugar de evidencia de causalidad; los estudios prospectivos deben determinar si la monitorización o corrección de anomalías de magnesio mejora los resultados de IC.

abstract_en: Abstract  Background  Transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis, a form of Cardiac Amyloidosis, is characterized by gradual accumulation of TTR, disrupting the anatomy and physiology of various organs, especially the heart; it has increasingly become a common cause of cardiac failure, morbidity, and mortality. Different genetic variants have been identified that are influenced by race and ethnicity, and the existing evidence affects treatment and clinical outcomes. However, the extent of this influence on the genetic variant is not fully understood. Methods  The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261404519) and conducted in line with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Six electronic databases were searched between June and July 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, CINAHL, ScienceDirect, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and 1,073 studies were retrieved. Following removal of duplicates, studies reporting race and ethnicity in confirmed ATTR-CM were included, and two independent reviewers screened the studies, assessed the risk of bias, and extracted the data. Data were synthesized narratively due to significant methodological differences. Results  941 out of 1,073 were screened, and 78 studies underwent full-text screening. 9 studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies showed a complex interplay between race/ethnicity and genetic carriage in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. p.V1421 mutations were significantly higher in black patients (79%) compared to white patients (1%). Invasive diagnostic tests are more common among the black patients compared to white counterparts (62.3 vs 17.7%), non - invasive techniques such as bone scintigraphy are more common with white patients (70.6% p = 0.016). Black patients with ATTRwt-CA, compared with non-black patients, received significantly lower disease-modifying therapy (68.4% vs 88.4%). More advanced forms of the disease, with higher risk of mortality, thromboembolism, heart failure, and frequent hospitalization, are more common with the black and Afro-Caribbean patients, although the disparities were absent or attenuated in some studies with more equitable access to treatment. Conclusion  Differences in race and ethnicity do exist in patients with confirmed ATTR-CM and involve genetic, diagnostic, and clinical outcomes. Genetic factors alone cannot fully explain these disparities and may reflect socioeconomic disadvantage and unequal healthcare access. Large multicenter studies are needed to explain these mechanisms and identify ways to reduce these disparities.

Resumen Antecedentes La amiloidosis transtiretina (TTR), una forma de amiloidosis cardíaca, se caracteriza por la acumulación gradual de TTR, que interrumpe la anatomía y fisiología de varios órganos, especialmente el corazón; se ha convertido cada vez más en una causa común de insuficiencia cardíaca, morbilidad y mortalidad. Se han identificado diferentes variantes genéticas que están influenciadas por la raza y la etnia, y la evidencia existente afecta el tratamiento y los resultados clínicos. Sin embargo, el alcance de esta influencia en la variante genética no se entiende plenamente. Métodos El protocolo de revisión se registró con PROSPERO (CRD420261404519) y se llevó a cabo de acuerdo con las directrices PRISMA 2020. Se buscaron seis bases de datos electrónicas entre junio y julio de 2026: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, CINAHL, ScienceDirect y Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), y se recuperaron 1.073 estudios. Tras la eliminación de duplicados, se incluyeron estudios que reportaban raza y etnia en ATTR-CM confirmados, y dos revisores independientes examinaron los estudios, evaluaron el riesgo de sesgo y extrajeron los datos.Los datos se sintetizaron narrativamente debido a diferencias metodológicas significativas.Los resultados fueron 941 de 1.073, y 78 estudios se sometieron a la revisión de texto completo. Estos estudios mostraron una interacción compleja entre raza/etnicidad y transporte genético en la amiloidosis cardíaca transtiretina. Las mutaciones en el V1421 fueron significativamente mayores en pacientes negros (79%) en comparación con los pacientes blancos (1%). Las pruebas diagnósticas invasivas son más frecuentes entre los pacientes negros en comparación con los pacientes blancos (62,3 vs 17,7%), las técnicas no invasivas como la centellografía ósea son más frecuentes en pacientes blancos (70,6% p = 0,016). Los pacientes negros con ATTRwt-CA, en comparación con los pacientes no negros, recibieron terapia modificativa de la enfermedad significativamente menor (68,4% vs 88,4%). Las formas más avanzadas de la enfermedad, con mayor riesgo de mortalidad, tromboembolismo, insuficiencia cardiaca y hospitalización frecuente, son más comunes con los pacientes negros y afrocaribeños, aunque las disparidades no se presentaron o se atenuaron en algunos estudios con acceso más equitativo al tratamiento. Conclusión Existen diferencias de raza y origen étnico en pacientes con ATTR-CM confirmados e involucran resultados genéticos, diagnósticos y clínicos. Los factores genéticos por sí solos no pueden explicar plenamente estas disparidades y pueden reflejar desventajas socioeconómicas y acceso desigual a la salud.

abstract_en:
Background
N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), patient-reported health status, and exercise capacity are commonly evaluated as measures of treatment response in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, it remains uncertain which treatment-induced changes show the strongest associations with treatment effects on major clinical events. We compared these associations in phase 3 ATTR-CM trials.Methods
We searched PubMed through September 30, 2026, for phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying ATTR-CM therapies. Random-effects meta-regression using restricted maximum likelihood assessed trial-level associations of treatment-induced changes in NT-proBNP, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OS), and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) with treatment effects on all-cause mortality, cardiovascular (CV) death, and recurrent CV events including CV-related hospitalizations and urgent heart failure visits. The log ratio of treatment-induced relative changes in NT-proBNP and between-group differences in KCCQ-OS and 6MWD were used as covariates. Weighted R2 and p-values from weighted regression and small-sample-corrected analyses were reported.Results
Five trials involving 3,520 participants were included. All five contributed to the analysis of all-cause mortality, whereas four contributed to analyses of CV death and recurrent CV events. Treatment-induced change in NT-proBNP showed the strongest trial-level association with treatment effects on recurrent CV events (weighted R2 = 0.955; β = 1.138; weighted regression p = 0.023; small-sample-corrected p = 0.106). No other associations were statistically significant.Conclusions
Our trial-level meta-regression identified the strongest association between treatment-induced changes in NT-proBNP and treatment effects on recurrent CV events, but this association was not statistically significant after small-sample correction. Given the small number of trials, this finding should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The observed association should be further evaluated in updated meta-regression analyses as results from ongoing ATTR-CM trials become available.

abstract_en: BackgroundTelehealth interventions for blood pressure (BP) monitoring and counselling are increasingly used to support follow-up care and long-term management in hypertension (HT). However, the comparative effectiveness of different telehealth feature combinations remains unclear.MethodsWe conducted a network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating telehealth monitoring interventions in adults with HT. Interventions were classified into four core digital health features: tracking (T), notify (N), remote (R) and educate (E). Intervention combinations included T, N, R, E, TN, TR, TE, NE, TNR, TNE, TRE, NRE and TNRE. Standard care (SC) served as the reference comparator. The primary outcome was controlled BP. Secondary outcomes were medication adherence and changes in systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP (DBP).ResultsForty RCTs involving 11,644 patients were included. Interventions incorporating more telehealth features were more effective than SC. For BP control, TNRE showed the highest odds of achieving control (OR 2.97, 95%CI 1.77-4.98), followed by TRE (OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.05-6.94). For medication adherence, only TNE showed a numerically greater effect, although the difference was not statistically significant, versus SC (SMD 3.36, 95%CI -0.43 to 7.15). For SBP, TNRE (MD -3.69 mmHg, 95%CI -7.00 to -0.38) and TNE (MD -3.83 mmHg, 95%CI -6.84 to -0.81) were associated with significant reductions versus SC. For DBP, only TNRE showed a significant reduction (MD -3.02 mmHg, 95%CI -5.30 to -0.74).ConclusionMulti-component telehealth interventions were associated with better BP outcomes than simpler approaches or SC. More integrated telehealth models may therefore offer greater benefit for HT follow-up.

Background:

 The primary objective of this systematic review is to assess the prevalence and percentage of increase/change of IOP after IVT. Secondary objectives include identifying risk factors for IOP change after IVT, practical guidelines for the management of increased IOP, and comparing the effects of different medications on IOP. Methods:
 A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for studies published between January 2020 and October 2025.  Intravitreal injections are associated with a significant but transient elevation in IOP, with the greatest increase occurring immediately after injection. Although IOP decreases over time, elevated levels may persist for up to one hour. abstract_en: Upper eyelid retraction is the most frequent sign of thyroid eye disease, yet surgical correction is deferred until the disease is quiescent, and systemic corticosteroids and targeted biologics carry appreciable toxicity and cost. We searched 4 databases to April, 2026, and pooled 12 studies (540 patients, 741 analytical units) evaluating local periocular triamcinolone acetonide injection, extracting only the triamcinolone arm of comparative trials. Injection lowered margin reflex distance-1 by a mean of 1.78 mm (95% CI, 1.20 to 2.35 mm) and produced clinical improvement in 87.0% of treated units (95% CI, 80.0% to 93.0%). Clinical activity score and proptosis did not change significantly. Transient ocular hypertension occurred in 4.0% and post-injection ptosis in 0.6% (95% CI, 0.2% to 2.0% by generalized linear mixed model). Certainty of evidence was very low to low throughout because all data derive from uncontrolled single-arm cohorts. Local triamcinolone injection is an inexpensive, accessible option for eyelid retraction during active disease, although controlled trials are lacking.

La retracción del párpado superior es el signo más frecuente de la enfermedad del ojo tiroideo, pero la corrección quirúrgica se pospone hasta que la enfermedad es quiescente, y los corticosteroides sistémicos y biológicos dirigidos conllevan toxicidad y costo apreciables. Se buscaron 4 bases de datos hasta abril de 2026, y se agruparon 12 estudios (540 pacientes, 741 unidades analíticas) para evaluar la inyección de acetonuro de triamcinolona periocular local, extrayendo sólo el brazo de triamcinolona de ensayos comparativos. La distancia del reflejo del margen de inyección bajada-1 por una media de 1,78 mm (IC 95%, 1,20 a 2,35 mm) y produjo mejoría clínica en el 87,0% de las unidades tratadas (IC 95%, 80,0% a 93,0%). abstract_en:
Objectives
To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the efficacy of remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) in improving claudication in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) compared with placebo or no intervention.Methods
We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases through June 24, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing RIPC with placebo or no intervention in patients with PAD, defined by an ankle-brachial index (ABI) ≤ 0.90 in association with clinical intermittent claudication (IC), up to Rutherford III or Fontaine IIB. The primary outcomes were changes from baseline in intermittent claudication distance (ICD) and maximum walking distance (MWD).Results
Six RCTs including 240 patients met the inclusion criteria; 122 patients (50.8%) received RIPC, whereas 118 patients (49.2%) received placebo or no intervention. RIPC was associated with greater changes from baseline in both ICD (MD 15.16 meters; 95% CI 8.65 to 21.68; P 2=0%) and MWD (MD 20.90 meters; 95% CI 10.65 to 31.15; P 2=0%). In the subgroup analysis including only trials using extended 28-day RIPC protocols, RIPC was also associated with significant improvements in ICD (MD 18.36 meters; 95% CI 1.33 to 35.39; P=0.03; I2=11%) and MWD (MD 20.88 meters; 95% CI 10.58 to 31.18; P 2=0%).Conclusion
In this systematic review and meta-analysis, RIPC was effective in improving claudication symptoms in patients with PAD. However, further clinical trials with well-established protocols and adequately powered sample sizes are needed before the routine clinical application of RIPC can be supported.

abstract_en: Abstract  Background and Aims:  Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common among patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and may adversely affect outcomes following catheter ablation. Although continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy has been associated with improved rhythm outcomes in observational studies, its effect remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between OSA and AF recurrence following catheter ablation and the association between CPAP therapy and recurrence among patients with OSA. Methods  Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Emcare were searched from inception to 27 September 2026 for studies reporting AF recurrence following catheter ablation according to OSA or CPAP treatment status. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation were performed to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, small-study effects, and sensitivity analyses were assessed. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Results  Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 19 studies comprising 5,748 patients contributed to the quantitative synthesis. OSA was associated with an increased risk of AF recurrence following catheter ablation across 16 studies (RR 1.43, 95% CI 1.30–1.58; I² = 16.3%), with a 95% prediction interval of 1.16–1.75. Among patients with OSA, CPAP use was associated with a lower risk of AF recurrence across eight studies (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.48–0.75; I² = 47.1%); however, the 95% prediction interval (0.33–1.09) included the null. Findings were stable in sensitivity analyses. Conclusion  OSA was associated with increased AF recurrence following catheter ablation. CPAP use was associated with lower recurrence among patients with OSA, although moderate heterogeneity, a prediction interval crossing unity, and predominantly observational evidence limit causal inference. Further adequately powered randomized trials are needed to determine whether CPAP directly improves post-ablation rhythm outcomes.

Resumen Antecedentes y objetivos: La apnea obstructiva del sueño (OSA) es común entre los pacientes con fibrilación auricular (AF) y puede afectar adversamente los resultados tras la ablación del catéter. Aunque la terapia con presión positiva continua de las vías respiratorias (CPAP) se ha asociado con mejores resultados del ritmo en estudios observacionales, su efecto sigue siendo incierto y se evaluó la asociación entre la APS y la recurrencia de la AF después de la ablación del catéter y la asociación entre la terapia con CPAP y la recurrencia entre los pacientes con AOS. Métodos Se realizó la búsqueda de Ovid MEDLINE, Embase y Emcare desde el inicio hasta el 27 de septiembre de 2026 para estudios que reportaron recurrencia de FA después de ablación del catéter de acuerdo con el estado de tratamiento de la AOS o CPAP. Se realizaron metaanálisis de efectos aleatorios mediante estimación de la máxima probabilidad restringida para calcular los coeficientes de riesgo agrupados (RRs) con intervalos de confianza del 95% (ICs), se evaluó la heterogeneidad, intervalos de predicción, efectos de estudio pequeños y análisis de sensibilidad, y se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando las herramientas del Índice Metodológico de Estudios No Randomizados y del Instituto Joanna Briggs. Resultados Veintidós estudios cumplieron con los criterios de inclusión, de los cuales 19 estudios con 5.748 pacientes contribuyeron a la síntesis cuantitativa; la AOS se asoció con un aumento del riesgo de recurrencia de FA después de la ablación del catéter en 16 estudios (RR 1,43, IC 95% 1,30–1,58; I2 = 16,3%), con un intervalo de predicción del 95% de 1,16–1,75; entre los pacientes con AOS, el uso de CPAP se asoció con un menor riesgo de recurrencia de FA en ocho estudios (RR 0,60, IC 95% 0,48–0,75; I2 = 47,1%); sin embargo, el intervalo de predicción del 95% (0,33–1,09) incluyó el nulo. Los hallazgos fueron estables en los análisis de sensibilidad. El uso de CPAP se asoció con menor recurrencia en pacientes con AOS, aunque heterogeneidad moderada, intervalo de predicción que cruza la unidad y evidencia predominantemente observacional que limita la inferencia causal. Se necesitan ensayos aleatorizados con potencia adecuada para determinar si el CPAP mejora directamente los resultados del ritmo post-ablación.

abstract_en: Abstract    Background  Interprofessional collaborative practice (ICP), including dietitians, is important for the care of obesity, diabetes and hypertension. However, evidence on the effectiveness of these practices for managing these conditions in adults and older adults is scarce. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of ICP involving dietitians in the management of hypertension, diabetes and/or obesity in adults and older adults through a systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods  A search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library databases on 28 April 2026, following the PRISMA guidelines. Studies that focused on ICP with dietitian involvement and that assessed glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and body mass index (BMI) were included. The meta-analysis was conducted with the randomized controlled trials using Jamovi software. A random-effects model was adopted, and the effect size was expressed as the mean difference with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I  2  statistic. Methodological quality was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, and publication bias with funnel plots and Egger's regression test, at a 5% significance level. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Results  Thirty articles were included in the systematic review, of which 10 (1,782 participants) were included in the meta-analysis. Several studies showed positive effects of ICP on the clinical and biochemical outcomes assessed. The meta-analysis showed that ICP reduced HbA1c (− 0.58; 95% CI − 1.00 to − 0.15; p = 0.008) and SBP (− 4.99; 95% CI − 9.89 to − 0.09; p = 0.046), but not BMI (− 1.22; 95% CI − 2.93 to 0.50; p = 0.164) or DBP (− 1.44; 95% CI − 4.18 to 1.30; p = 0.303). All outcomes showed high heterogeneity (I  2   > 75%). Conclusions  ICP showed favorable results in the management of diabetes, hypertension and obesity. The meta-analysis indicated the effectiveness of these interventions in reducing HbA1c and SBP. These findings highlight the relevance of interprofessional work, including dietitians, in the care of chronic diseases.

Resumen Antecedentes La práctica colaborativa interprofesional (PCI), incluyendo a los dietistas, es importante para el cuidado de la obesidad, diabetes e hipertensión, pero es escasa la evidencia de la efectividad de estas prácticas para el manejo de estas condiciones en adultos y adultos mayores, con el objetivo de analizar la efectividad de la PCI involucrando a los dietistas en el manejo de la hipertensión, diabetes y/o obesidad en adultos y adultos mayores a través de una revisión sistemática y metaanálisis. Métodos Se realizó una búsqueda en las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, Scopus, Web of Science y Cochrane Library el 28 de abril de 2026, siguiendo las directrices PRISMA. Se incluyeron estudios que se enfocaron en la PCI con compromiso dietista y que evaluaron la hemoglobina glicada (HbA1c), la presión arterial sistólica (PAS) y la presión arterial diastólica (PAD) e índice de masa corporal (IMC). El metaanálisis se realizó con los ensayos controlados aleatorizados utilizando el software Jamovi. Se adoptó un modelo de efectos aleatorios, y el tamaño del efecto se expresó como la diferencia media con intervalos de confianza del 95% (IC 95%). La heterogeneidad se evaluó utilizando la estadística I 2; la calidad metodológica se evaluó con las herramientas de evaluación crítica del Instituto Joanna Briggs, y el sesgo de publicación con tramas de embudo y la prueba de regresión de Egger, a un nivel de significación del 5%. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo con la herramienta Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, se incluyeron 30 artículos en la revisión sistemática, de los cuales 10 (1.782 participantes) fueron incluidos en el metaanálisis, y varios estudios mostraron efectos positivos de la PCI en los resultados clínicos y bioquímicos evaluados; el metaanálisis mostró que la PCI redujo la HbA1c (− 0,58; IC 95% − 1,00 a 0,15; p = 0,008) y la PAS (− 4,99; IC 95% − 9,89 a − 0,09; p = 0,046), pero no el IMC (− 1,22; IC 95% − 2,93 a 0,50; p = 0,164) o la PAD (− 1,44; IC 95% − 4,18 a 1,30; p = 0,303). Todos los resultados mostraron una alta heterogeneidad (I 2 > 75%). Conclusiones El PCI mostró resultados favorables en el manejo de la diabetes, la hipertensión y la obesidad, y el metaanálisis indicó la efectividad de estas intervenciones en la reducción de la HbA1c y la PAS. Estos hallazgos destacan la relevancia del trabajo interprofesional, incluyendo a los dietistas, en el cuidado de enfermedades crónicas.

abstract_en:
Background
Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR).Methods
We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated.Results
Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29).Conclusions
Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

abstract_en: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) creates myocardial lesions with brief, nonthermal electrical pulses. We synthesized randomized comparisons of PFA with radiofrequency and cryoballoon ablation for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through October 13, 2026. We included randomized trials enrolling adults with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and comparing PFA with thermal ablation. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios and mean differences. Leave-one-out and Baujat analyses examined sensitivity and heterogeneity. Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Four randomized trials, reported in 6 publications, enrolled 1396 participants. For 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia, the 4-trial analysis (n=1392) found no significant difference (risk ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval, 0.92-1.17; P=0.374; I2=3.6%). Reconstructed data comprised 1368 participants and 423 recurrences. Estimated 12-month freedom from recurrence was 70.6% with PFA and 66.7% with thermal ablation (log-rank p=0.097; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.02). Procedure time was numerically lower with PFA, but the pooled result was nonsignificant and heterogeneous. Fluoroscopy time did not differ significantly; left atrial dwell time was shorter with substantial heterogeneity. No safety outcome differed significantly, and no atrioesophageal fistulas were reported. Randomized evidence indicates similar short-term efficacy for PFA and thermal ablation. The reconstructed survival analysis favored PFA numerically but did not establish a difference.
abstract_es: Abstract

La ablación de campo pulsado (PFA) crea lesiones miocárdicas con pulsos eléctricos breves y no térmicos. Se sintetizaron comparaciones aleatorias de AFP con radiofrecuencia y ablación criobalona para aislamiento venoso pulmonar en fibrilación auricular paroxística (AF). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, y la Biblioteca Cochrane fueron buscados desde el inicio hasta el 13 de octubre de 2026. Se incluyeron ensayos aleatorizados que incluyeron adultos con fibrilación auricular paroxística y comparando AFP con ablación térmica. Modelos de efectos aleatorios agruparon relaciones de riesgo y diferencias medias. Los datos de tiempo a evento fueron reconstruidos a partir de las curvas de Kaplan-Meier publicadas. Cuatro ensayos aleatorizados, reportados en 6 publicaciones, incluyeron a 1396 participantes. Para 12 meses libres de arritmia auricular, el análisis de 4 ensayos (n=1392) no encontró diferencia significativa (razón de riesgo 1,04, intervalo de confianza 95%, 0,92-1,17; P=0,374; I2=3,6%). Los datos reconstruidos comprendieron 1368 participantes y 423 recurrencias. La libertad estimada de 12 meses de recurrencia fue 70,6% con AFP y 66,7% con ablación térmica (log-rango p=0,097; hazard ratio 0,84, intervalo de confianza 95%, 0,70-1,02). El tiempo de procedimiento fue numéricamente menor con AFP, pero el resultado combinado fue no significativo y heterogéneo. El tiempo de fluoroscopia no difirió significativamente; el tiempo de permanencia en el atrial izquierdo fue más corto con una heterogeneidad sustancial; ningún resultado de seguridad difirió significativamente, y no se reportaron fístulas auriesofágicas; la evidencia aleatoria indica una eficacia similar a corto plazo para la AFP y la ablación térmica; el análisis de supervivencia reconstruido favoreció la AFP numéricamente pero no estableció diferencia.

abstract_en:
Background
Patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² presents unique clinical challenges, often requiring highly effective metabolic and bariatric interventions to achieve substantial weight reduction and obesity-associated medical conditions remission. Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) remains the most frequently performed procedure globally due to its technical simplicity and favorable short-term safety. However, long-term concerns regarding recurrent weight gain (RWG) and suboptimal clinical response (SoCR) in patients with higher baseline BMIs persist. One anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) has emerged as a powerful alternative, combining both restrictive and intestinal-rerouting mechanisms to optimize metabolic outcomes. Despite its growing popularity, head-to-head evidence directly comparing the long-term efficacy, safety profiles, and complication rates of OAGB versus SG specifically within patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² demographic remains limited.Objective
To compare the mid-term efficacy, safety profile, and resolution of metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions between one anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) and sleeve gastrectomy (SG) in patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m².Methods
We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane through January 2026. Primary endpoint was total weight loss (%TWL). Secondary endpoints were remission of type 2 diabetes (T2D), hypertension remission, and rate of reoperation. Data was pooled using RevMan 5.4, evaluating Risk Ratios (RR) for dichotomous variables and Mean Differences (MD) for continuous variables, with 95% Confidence Intervals (CI).Results
Eleven studies encompassing a total of 2,539 patients were included in the final review. The pooled analysis demonstrated that OAGB yielded a statistically significant superior Total Weight Loss compared to SG (MD = 9.56; 95% CI [9.01, 10.11]; p Conclusion
In patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m², OAGB provides significantly greater total weight loss compared to SG. Both procedures demonstrate comparable safety profiles and similar effectiveness in the remission of major metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions. OAGB is a highly effective and safe alternative for managing obesity.

abstract_en:
Background
The DIG-Mod HF trial is the first trial to evaluate the mechanistic effects of low-dose digoxin on myocardial work and functional exercise capacity in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction receiving contemporary guideline-recommended medical therapy (GRMT). Although a recent meta-analysis demonstrated clinical benefit of cardiac glycosides in addition to contemporary GRMT, the mechanistic basis for this effect remains unexplored.Objectives
The authors aimed to investigate whether low-dose digoxin improves myocardial work and functional exercise capacity when added to optimized GRMT.Methods
An open-label, randomized crossover trial enrolled 50 patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction on maximally tolerated GRMT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to digoxin 0.125 mg/day plus standard of care or standard of care alone, each for 24 weeks, for a total study duration of 48 weeks. Co-primary endpoints were within-patient changes in peak oxygen consumption (Vo2) and left ventricular global work index.Results
The study population was highly optimized, with 88% in NYHA functional class II on near-universal quadruple GRMT. Digoxin did not significantly improve peak Vo2 (mean difference: -0.08 mL/kg/min; 95% CI: -1.64 to 1.47 mL/kg/min; P = 0.914). Global work index improved significantly (mean difference: 157.8 mm Hg%; 95% CI: 12.2-303.4 mm Hg%; P = 0.034). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12 score also improved during the digoxin period. The composite safety endpoint did not differ significantly between arms (P = 0.089).Conclusions
Low-dose digoxin significantly improved myocardial work without improving peak Vo2. Demonstrating these effects in a clinically stable, well-treated population is consistent with an independent pharmacologic effect of digoxin in addition to modern guideline-directed therapy. (Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment [DIG-Mod HF]; EU Clinical Trials Register Number: 2024-513448-26-00).

title: Early defibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A systematic synthesis of the time-dependent decline of shockable rhythms.
short: Early defibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A systematic synthesis of the time-dependent decline of shockable rhythms.
summary: Esta revisión sistemática tuvo como objetivo sintetizar evidencia sobre cómo los ritmos shockables disminuyen con el tiempo en el paro cardíaco extrahospitalario (OHCA) de adultos y examinar cómo el tiempo de desfibrilación se relaciona con el deterioro del ritmo y los resultados clínicos. abstract_en: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on how shockable rhythms decline over time in adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and to examine how defibrillation timing relates to rhythm deterioration and clinical outcomes. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for studies reporting initial rhythm distribution and time-to-defibrillation or untreated arrest duration in adult OHCA. Observational cohorts, registry-based studies, physiological waveform analyses, and randomized trials were included. Data were extracted on rhythm prevalence, time-related measures, defibrillation success, and clinical outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools. Thirty-eight studies published between 1990 and 2025 were included, encompassing more than 262,700 OHCA cases. Among unselected cohorts, the median prevalence of initial shockable rhythms was 33.5% (IQR 22.6-42.8%). Across study designs, increasing time-to-defibrillation was consistently associated with decreasing shockable rhythm prevalence and progressive transition to non-shockable rhythms. Physiological and AED waveform analyses demonstrated progressive deterioration of ventricular fibrillation with increasing untreated duration. Early defibrillation was associated with higher defibrillation success, increased return of spontaneous circulation, and improved survival outcomes. Shockable rhythms decline progressively with increasing untreated arrest duration, reflecting time-dependent electrical deterioration from ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia to non-shockable rhythms. These findings support the concept of a limited early shockable window in cardiac arrest and reinforce the critical importance of minimizing time-to-defibrillation across emergency response systems to improve survival in OHCA.
abstract_es: Abstract

Esta revisión sistemática tuvo como objetivo sintetizar evidencia sobre cómo los ritmos shockables disminuyen con el tiempo en el paro cardíaco extrahospitalario (OHCA) de adultos y examinar cómo el tiempo de desfibrilación se relaciona con el deterioro del ritmo y los resultados clínicos. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de acuerdo con las directrices PRISMA. Se buscaron bases de datos electrónicas para estudios que reportan distribución inicial del ritmo y duración del tiempo de desfibrilación o de parada no tratada en adultos OHCA. Se incluyeron cohortes observacionales, estudios basados en registros, análisis fisiológicos de forma de onda y ensayos aleatorizados. Se evaluó el riesgo de sesgo utilizando herramientas RoB 2 y ROBINS-I. Se incluyeron 38 estudios publicados entre 1990 y 2025, que abarcaron más de 262.700 casos de OHCA. Entre las cohortes no seleccionadas, la prevalencia mediana de ritmos shockables iniciales fue del 33,5% (IQR 22.6-42,8 %). En los diseños del estudio, el aumento del tiempo hasta la desfibrilación se asoció consistentemente con la disminución de la prevalencia del ritmo shockable y la transición progresiva a ritmos no shockables. La desfibrilación temprana se asoció con un mayor éxito en la desfibrilación, un mayor retorno de la circulación espontánea y mejores resultados de supervivencia.Los ritmos escandalosos disminuyen progresivamente con el aumento de la duración del paro no tratado, reflejando el deterioro eléctrico dependiente del tiempo desde la fibrilación ventricular o la taquicardia ventricular sin pulso hasta los ritmos no escandalosos.Estos hallazgos apoyan el concepto de una ventana de choque precoz limitada en el paro cardíaco y refuerzan la importancia crítica de minimizar el tiempo hasta la desfibrilación en los sistemas de respuesta de emergencia para mejorar la supervivencia en el AHO.
